children: MUFG Bank Ltd. aims to "actively pursue collaboration on such matters as (increasing) customer touchpoints" with non-financial sectors, said President and CEO Masakazu Osawa during an interview with The Yomiuri Shimbun.
"It is entirely possible that we will partner with sectors such as distribution," he added.
The following is excerpted from the interview.
The Yomiuri Shimbun: What areas do you plan to focus on?

Masakazu Osawa: Regarding individual customers, I feel that the mindset of "shifting from savings to investment" is becoming firmly established, particularly among the younger generation who are in their 20s and 30s. Funds are not merely being deposited but are also flowing into NISA (Nippon Individual Savings Account, a tax-free program for small investments) and credit card investment services, for example. We want to capitalize on this trend through "M-tto," a comprehensive financial service for individual customers of Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group Inc.

With regard to corporate clients, I believe support for companies is essential in order for Japanese technology to be reestablished on the global stage. Japanese-made semiconductors, electronics and software have the potential to play a crucial role in global supply chains.

Awareness of (the importance of) economic security is also growing, and we want to support efforts to strengthen domestic supply capabilities. There is significant room for growth, including in the aviation and aerospace sectors as well as in film and other areas of the media industry.
Yomiuri: What are your expectations for the company's digital bank?

Osawa: We aim to launch a digital bank utilizing M-tto next year. We are concerned about the shift of money deposited by individual customers to online banks, particularly at times such as when inheritances are being settled. Competition for deposits is intensifying, and traditional banking systems simply cannot compete in some respects. We want to explore what kind of added value we can provide to customers through the digital bank.

The planned digital bank will be able to flexibly adjust fees and interest rates based on customer attributes and service usage patterns. We aim to create a system where customers benefit more the more they use our group's products and services.
Yomiuri: Given the shift from savings to investment, how do you view collaboration with securities services?

Osawa: In conjunction with the launch of the digital bank, we want to further strengthen collaboration with online brokerage operations. Including through the use of apps, we aim to create a seamless, integrated user experience that eliminates the feeling that there is a barrier between digital banking and brokerage app services (although there are regulatory constraints).
Yomiuri: What is your view on collaboration with non-financial sectors?
Osawa: We will actively pursue collaboration on such matters as (increasing) customer touchpoints. It is entirely possible that we will partner with sectors such as distribution.
